text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"Large trials in vitamin D-replete adults found no reduction in cancer, cardiovascular events, falls, fractures, or type 2 diabetes.","cited_pids":["fbce4d7a6120#1","fbce4d7a6120#3","0dafa2c8c11c#3","d8b33533d51c#3"]},{"cid":"c2","text":"A high-dose vitamin D trial found lower radial bone density without a bone strength benefit.","cited_pids":["8f7161b0be98#5"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"Systematic reviews reach a consensus that vitamin D supplementation provides no fracture benefit.","cited_pids":["53bc338e3607#5"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"An Endocrine Society guideline suggests empiric vitamin D supplementation for adults aged 75 and older, pregnant women, and those with high-risk prediabetes.","cited_pids":["8279771cfc3d#4"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"Post hoc analyses suggest some extra-skeletal benefits of vitamin D supplementation in people with deficiency.","cited_pids":["fbce4d7a6120#3"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"Vitamin D supplementation guidance targets specific groups and deficiency rather than universal daily use.","cited_pids":["8279771cfc3d#0"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"The strength of the benefit of vitamin D supplementation for targeted groups is uncertain.","cited_pids":["8279771cfc3d#0"]}]}
